newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ifo says EMU will hurt, then help EU employment. [corrected 15:10 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Ifo says EMU will hurt, then help EU employment. [corrected 15:10 gmt]

text.p: European unemployment levels will rise in the short term as governments engage in cost-cutting to meet Maastricht entry goals for economic and monetary union (EMU), Germany's Ifo institute said on Tuesday.

Further down the line, the currency union will help to create more jobs in Europe, but additional economic and wage policy measures are needed, particularly in Germany, to bring this about, the economic research intsitute said.
Ifo cited data from the research body Barrel, Morgan and Pain, which showed that another 24,000 jobs would be lost in Germany and 500,000 shed in the EU as a whole by the year 2000.
(Corrects to make clear the data were not Ifo's own, but used by Ifo to illustrate its employment outlook).
Beyond the year 2000, the data showed unemployment levels in the region declining.
Ifo said that even after the introduction of the euro, scheduled for January 1999, employment levels would suffer in the near term due to economic setbacks.
Beyond then, however, efficiency and growth improvements coupled with the elimination of exchange rate fluctuations will have a positive impact on economies, Ifo said.

The institute said price stability should be of paramount importance in policy-setting after the introduction of a single currency, adding that if this stability was credible in the eyes of financial markets, higher rates of employment and domestic production could be achieved.
The euro will also prompt large changes in wage negotiations, Ifo said, since wage talks would also become international talks with employees elsewhere in the union also being paid in euro.

It said that trade unions would become more involved in the economic rivalry between nations and regions, adding that the aim of employment negotiations would not only focus on the distribution of work, but also on ensuring job creation and job security.
